load_frame_image(frame_path, target_width)[source]

Load an image from the given path and resize it to the target width. This method uses PIL to load and resize the image, then converts it to QPixmap. This is done to avoid issues with QPixmap loading large images directly.

Parameters:

  • frame_path – Path to the image file

  • target_width – Target width for resizing the image

Returns:

Resized image as QPixmap

Return type:

QPixmap

open_in_system_player()[source]

Opne the video at the current frame in the system’s default video player. This will attempt to use commonly used Ubuntu video players that support seeking to a specific timestamp and open the video.

If none are found, it will fall back to xdg-open which will open the video in the default video player, but not at the specific timestamp.

deduplicate_tracker_results(results, max_frames_interval=15)[source]

Deduplicate results based on tracked object IDs and classes, but keep frames with new objects

Parameters:

  • results (dict) – Dictionary of frame paths and detection lists

  • max_frames_interval (int) – Maximum number of frames to skip before forcing inclusion

Returns:

Dictionary of unique frames with detections

Return type:

dict

deduplicate_yolo_results(results, min_count_change=1, max_frames_interval=8, min_confidence=0.1)[source]

Deduplicate results based on object classes, counts, and color names. Filter out frames that don’t contain significant changes, but keep important frames.

Parameters:

  • results (dict) – Dictionary of frame paths and detection lists

  • min_count_change (int) – Minimum count change to consider a frame significant

  • max_frames_interval (int) – Maximum number of frames to skip before forcing inclusion

  • min_confidence (float) – Minimum confidence score to consider a detection valid

Returns:

Dictionary of unique frames with detections

Return type:

dict

run()[source]

run()

Run the worker thread to process the video. This method is executed in a separate thread. It emits the finished signal when processing is complete, or the error signal if an error occurs.
